name: Non-Contrast Computed Tomography
description: Non-contrast computed tomography scanning (CT scans) is a type of X-ray imaging technique that is used to diagnosis and locate first and recurrent subarachnoid hemorrhage (rebleeding).
description_reference: van Gijn J, and van Dongen KJ. Computed Tomography in the Diagnosis of Subarachnoid Haemorrhage and Ruptured Aneurysm. Clinical Neurology and Neurosurgery, 1980; 82: 11–24. https://doi.org/10.1016/0303-8467(80)90055-4

name: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
description: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an imaging technique that uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves to produce detailed images of the brain. Following aSAH, MRI can be used to identify the presence, location, and extent of new or recurrent bleeding.

name: Clinical Assessment
description: Clinical assessment involves monitoring a patient for changes on a neurological examination, such as a sudden decrease in level of consciousness, new weakness, or speech difficulties. A sudden rise in intracranial pressure may also raise concern for rebleeding. These clinical changes can help signal that rebleeding or another problem may have occured, but imaging is usually needed to confirm the cause.

name: Cerebrospinal Fluid Spectrophotometry
status_rationale: CSF spectrophotometry can not distinguish the initial aSAH event from a distinct second instance of rebleeding. Working Group Leads level of agreement: 100 % (3/3).
description: CSF spectrophotometry is a quantitative method used to measure and follow xanthochromia (the yellow-pigmented cerebrospinal fluid that follows a subarachnoid hemorrhage). It provides a sensitive index that helps clinicians diagnose a subarachnoid hemorrhage and differentiate it from a traumatic lumbar puncture.
description_reference: Tsementzis SA, Hitchcock ER, DeCothi A, et al. Comparative Studies of the Diagnostic Value of Cerebrospinal Fluid Spectrophotometry and Computed Tomographic Scanning in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage. Neurosurgery 1985; 17: 908–12. https://doi.org/10.1227/00006123-198512000-00007

name: Convolutional Neural Networks
status_rationale: Convolution Neural Networks are not commonly available across treatment centres worldwide. Working Group Leads level of agreement: 100 % (3/3).
description: A convolutional neural network is an AI tool trained to identify bleeding on medical scans. It highlights areas that may contain blood and can help clinicians detect, locate, and classify hemorrhage.
description_reference: Barros RS, van der Steen WE, Boers AMM, et al. Automated Segmentation of Subarachnoid Hemorrhages with Convolutional Neural Networks. Informatics in Medicine Unlocked 2020; 19. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.imu.2020.100321
